werde.es: llegue a ser, vaya a (Konjunktiv I de «werden»)

texto: It forms with the root of the verb plus the **-e, -est, -e, -en, -et, -en** terminations: **er komme** (says it comes), **sie habe** (says it has). Only the singular and the third person are common. The verb **sein** is the most important: **ich sei, du seiest, er sei, wir seien, ihr seiet, sie seien**.
With **haben** and **werden** also: **er habe**, **er werde**. The other verbs form the same.

It is used to present other words: **Er sagt, er sei krank** / **Er sagt, dass er krank sei**. Without **dass**, the conjugated verb usually occupies the second position; with **dass**, it goes to the end. The Konjunktiv I marks the speech referred to, not the time: this is understood by the verbal form and context. It does not imply that anyone who reports doubts what has been said.

filas: Sie sagt, sie habe keine Zeit.

frases.de: Die Polizei teilt mit, der Unfall sei am Morgen passiert.
frases.es: La policía informa de que el accidente ocurrió por la mañana.
frases.en: The police report the accident happened in the morning.

frases.de: Zuerst hieß es, es gebe keine Verletzten.
frases.es: Al principio se dijo que no había heridos.
frases.en: At first it was said that there were no injuries.

frases.de: Später erklärte das Ministerium, es werde neue Regeln geben.
frases.es: Más tarde, el ministerio explicó que habría nuevas normas.
frases.en: Later, the ministry explained that there would be new rules.

frases.de: Eine Statistik zeige, die Zahl der Verletzten sei gesunken.
frases.es: Una estadística muestra que el número de heridos ha bajado.
frases.en: A statistic shows that the number of injured has fallen.

frases.de: Experten prüfen jetzt, ob die neuen Regeln helfen.
frases.es: Ahora los expertos comprueban si las nuevas normas ayudan.
frases.en: Experts now check whether the new standards help.

bloques.pregunta: According to the news, what do the experts want to check?

opciones.explicacion: The last sentence says they're checking if the rules help.

opciones.texto: If the police published a statistic.
opciones.explicacion: The statistics are already on the news.

opciones.texto: If the accident was in the morning.
opciones.explicacion: The news reports when it happened, not what they're investigating now.

bloques.pregunta: What form of «sein» is correct for «He says he's sick.» (Konjunktiv I)?

opciones.explicacion: It is Indikative: it is not used in indirect style.

bloques.pregunta: What form is «She says she has time.»?

opciones.explicacion: The main verb would be past.

bloques.frase: Die Polizei teilt mit, der Unfall ___ harmlos.

bloques.pregunta: What does this official announcement report?
bloques.frase: Das Ministerium erklärt, es werde neue Regeln geben.

opciones.texto: The ministry explains that there will be new rules.
opciones.explicacion: «werde ... geben» is the future Konjunktiv I in neutral indirect style.

opciones.texto: The ministry confirms that the new rules have already failed.
opciones.explicacion: The text indicates that they will be implemented, not that they have failed.

opciones.texto: The Ministry calls for no rules to be applied in the investigation.
opciones.explicacion: This is not a negative request, but a regulatory announcement.

bloques.pregunta: What main verb is usually used in the news to introduce an indirect style?
How is it expressed in neutral indirect style «She says she has time.»?

opciones.explicacion: In a formal indirect style with the 3rd person singular the Konjunktiv I «habe» is used.
The «hat» sign does not mark a journalistic distance or a speech.

opciones.texto: Sie sagt, sie hätte Zeit gehabt.
opciones.explicacion: It is Konjunktiv II in the past («I would have had time.»), altering verbal time.

intro: We started level B2 with a new form: the **Konjunktiv I**. It serves to tell what someone else has said, without giving our opinion. It's very typical of the newspapers and the news.
